routes.label: Check the three possible oldest people against the truth count

question:
Amy, Bill and Celine are friends with different ages. Exactly one of the following statements is true.

\(\mathrm{I}.\) Bill is the oldest.

\(\mathrm{II}.\) Amy is not the oldest.

\(\mathrm{III}.\) Celine is not the youngest.

Rank the friends from the oldest to youngest.
solution:
Exactly one statement is true, so any age order that makes two statements true is impossible.

If Bill were oldest, statement I would be true, and statement II would also be true because Amy would not be oldest. If Celine were oldest, statements II and III would both be true. Thus neither Bill nor Celine can be oldest, so Amy must be oldest.

Now statements I and II are false, so statement III must be true: Celine is not youngest. Since Amy is oldest and the ages are different, Celine must be in the middle and Bill must be youngest. The order is Amy, Celine, Bill, choice E.
